rowText: Standing row (docs/testing-manual.md "QA-FREE-PLAY-01"): run after ANY change to the Main tab's layout, scrolling, focus graph, or the dock, before the change is called verified. Every stop must be focused AND visible; a section arriving mid-stream must not steal focus or leave a focused stop hidden. The streaming half (walk while the reply is still writing) has been owed since 2026-09-16 and was still owed after the 2026-09-18 01:05-01:55 run because the device time went to the cache-clear attempt instead.

settings.ask_think_effort: high (raised from medium for this run)

setup.pinnedChip: give me a very long, detailed guide to getting the most battery life out of my Steam Deck, covering every setting that matters, with a section for each setting and examples (the box truncates the stored chip at the 160-character sanitizer cap, so the sentence that was actually sent reads "...with a section for each setting", no "and examples")

steps.press: A on the pinned chip, then A on ask
steps.landing: ask button greyed/disabled, reply streaming (log: POST 08:43:38, stream done 08:44:40, 62.0s total)

steps.press: deck_sweep DOWN returnTrip:true from the top of the pane, started ~9s into the still-streaming reply
steps.expected: every stop focused and visible, no dead ends
steps.landing: 8 distinct stops visited over 14 presses (2 legs); 6 of the 8 stops were FOCUSED BUT NOT VISIBLE (all offscreen except one 33% partial, covered by the ask box) because the transcript kept growing and auto-scrolling under the ring while the sweep walked; the DOWN leg also looped (Retry -> <div> -> "Show reasoning · 19s" -> <div> -> Retry, escaped:false) and stopped itself rather than reaching further into the still-arriving text

verdictSentence: While the answer was still being written, the D-pad ring got stuck focused on controls a person could not see on screen six times out of eight stops, because the growing reply pushed the page around faster than the ring could keep up; a person walking the pane with a controller while an answer streams would lose track of where they are.
